picks.name: The Affluent Classic
picks.why_plausible: Price_sensitivity: low, high-AOV infrequent buyer who values 'quality and longevity over trends' — exactly the buyer for a $1,200 made-to-order Florentine bag. Her messaging preferences (craftsmanship, heritage, understated) map directly to the brand's stated heritage and handcrafted claims.
lean_into: handcrafted in Florence by Italian artisans
a bag made to last, not to trend
picks.ad_angle: Old-world Florentine craftsmanship: one artisan, six weeks, a bag you'll carry for decades.

picks.name: The Gifter
picks.why_plausible: The brief lists gift as a secondary occasion, and this persona is a low-price-sensitivity mode buyer hunting 'impressive-looking' purchases. A custom-fit Italian leather bag is a high-impact milestone gift — and the 6-week lead time suits planned life events.
lean_into: made-to-order personalization as the thoughtful touch
plan ahead: order six weeks before the occasion
avoid: last-minute shipping promises the brand can't make
picks.ad_angle: The milestone gift you commission, not buy off a shelf — order six weeks ahead of the anniversary or birthday.

picks.name: The Gen Z Aesthete
picks.why_plausible: Female-leaning fashion and small_batch affinity with strong aesthetic-forward, values-aligned preferences fits a Florence atelier's story. Price_sensitivity medium-high makes this a stretch, so treat it as aspirational/saved-for purchase rather than impulse.
lean_into: aesthetic-forward visuals of the atelier and leather
a brand that stands for something: small-batch, human-made
custom-fit as self-expression, your spec not a mass drop
picks.ad_angle: Anti-mass-market: your bag, built to your spec in a small Florence workshop — the opposite of a drop.

creative.angle: Old-world Florentine craftsmanship over speed — a made-to-order bag built to be carried for decades
creative.headline: Handcrafted in Florence. Six weeks.
creative.body: A leather handbag made to your fit, by hand in Italy. It ships in about six weeks because that's how long it takes. Around $1,200.
creative.offer_suggestion: Offer a complimentary leather swatch set or a personal fitting consultation before ordering — no discount framing.
creative.tone_notes: Understated, declarative sentences and no exclamation or trend language. Leads with place and craft, treats the six-week wait as evidence of care rather than a drawback, and states price plainly since price sensitivity is low.

plan.summary: No true luxury-accessory publisher exists in this catalog, so the plan narrows to two high-income mature women's apparel tests (Marlowe & Co., Linden Park) while everything else falls out on category or a 10-40x price gap.

test.name: Marlowe & Co.
test.adjustment_reason: Notes say the audience 'Responds to quality messaging' and has 'Lower impulse but high AOV', which directly offsets the raw price-gap penalty for a craftsmanship-led luxury offer.
test.rationale: Marlowe's 45-65, 96% female, high-income base is the closest thing in the catalog to affluent buyers of handcrafted Italian leather, and its notes explicitly say shoppers respond to quality messaging rather than impulse.

evidence.quote: Older affluent women. Lower impulse but high AOV

test.risk: A $1,200 made-to-order bag is roughly 10x the $112 typical order, and the six-week wait will thin conversion even among interested shoppers.

test.name: Linden Park
test.adjustment_reason: Notes flag it as the 'Highest-AOV apparel publisher in the catalog' with a 'Conservative brand sensibility', both of which favour a heritage, classic-leather pitch more than the price signal alone suggests.
test.rationale: Linden Park's 50-70, 98% female, high-income readers of classic and workwear brands map onto timeless Italian leather, and its conservative sensibility suits heritage-and-craft copy.

evidence.quote: Highest-AOV apparel publisher in the catalog

test.risk: Smallest reach of the two apparel tests at 6.2M impressions, and the $128 typical order is still ~9x below the offer price.

bid_strategy.rationale: $1,200 first order × 0.30 = $360.00 target CPA: one-time purchase, so the first order has to pay back the acquisition. The max CPA allows headroom while the campaign learns over 14 days.

frequency_cap.rationale: Offers appear once, right after checkout; repeating them reads as spam.

experiment.graduate_rule: After 14 days, move a test publisher to core if its CPA is at or below target; cut any placement above max CPA.
experiment.notes: Creatives rotate evenly until each has enough conversions to compare.

assumptions: We assumed the main buyer is women aged roughly 30-60, since the brief does not say.
We assumed it's a one-time purchase, not a subscription.
Allowable CPA is 30% of first order value (one time); replace with real margin and LTV.
warnings: No publisher cleared the recommended bar, so the whole budget is a test. Treat results as exploratory.
